clue.text: Lawmen — or sergeant neatly arrayed

indicators.note: arrayed means set out in a new order, so the three words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Police officers, or perhaps a smartly turned-out sergeant, are paraded in line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neatly' looks like it describes how the sergeant is arrayed, but it is part of the anagram fodder with OR and SERGEANT.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief law officers of governments are senior legal figures, loosely lawmen.

clue.text: Familiar reception

definitions.meaning: at ease, comfortable, as one is in one's own house
a party held in one's own house for visitors

explanation.definitionFit: To be relaxed somewhere is to feel at ease there; an informal party given in a private house bears the same name.

clue.text: In France you encountered Diana with the royal family

indicators.note: encountered means meeting, so the two pieces are placed side by side

parts.note: tu is the familiar French word for you
Diana Dors was a British film actress of the 1950s

explanation.surface: A French friend bumped into Diana while out with the royals.
explanation.definitionFit: The English ruling house from Henry VII to Elizabeth I was a royal dynasty.

clue.text: Note about means of curdling milk

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for the note is read backwards

parts.note: a tenner is a ten-pound banknote

explanation.surface: A memo concerns how to make milk curdle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' suggests music or a written memo; it is a banknote, a TENNER (British slang for a ten-pound note).
explanation.definitionFit: This enzyme preparation from calves' stomachs is used to curdle milk in cheesemaking.

clue.text: Country rock saved a roll

indicators.note: rock means shake or disturb, so these letters are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: Country and rock music rescued a roll of the drums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' and 'rock' read as music genres; 'Country' is the definition and 'rock' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A small Central American republic is a nation.

clue.text: If animal and bird go to church, it's for turning nuts

parts.note: a monkey is a kind of animal
a wren is a small bird

explanation.surface: Some odd instruction about animals and birds attending church to deal with nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' suggests something to eat or eccentric people; it means the metal nuts on bolts.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjustable spanner is a tool for gripping and turning bolts.

clue.text: Deadlines when travelling out by air?

indicators.note: travelling means moving about, so the letters of the phrase are moved around

explanation.surface: Flight times out by plane, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deadlines' looks like time limits; read as dead lines, it means lines written about the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A published death notice consists of lines written about someone deceased.

clue.text: They finally cast off torn net skirt

indicators.note: torn means ripped apart, so the letters of the phrase are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Some people at last discard a ripped tulle skirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast off' looks like discarding the torn skirt; it is the knitting term for finishing work, which needle workers do last.
explanation.definitionFit: People working wool on needles end each piece by casting off the stitches.

clue.text: Rovers player knocked up by knight now playing in Virginia

indicators.note: by means next to, so the knight's letters stand beside the player
knocked up means pushed upwards, and in a down clue that reads the name from bottom to top

parts.note: Roy of the Rovers is a British comic-strip footballer

indicators.note: playing means in action, so the letters of the word now are rearranged

explanation.surface: A footballer is battered by a knight who is now playing in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rovers player' is the hero of the British comic strip Roy of the Rovers; 'knocked up' reverses him in this down entry. The definition is a place found 'in Virginia', the 1781 battlefield.
explanation.definitionFit: The site of the 1781 British surrender is a historic town on the York River in that US state.

clue.text: Fellow involved in robbery is a pleasure-seeker

indicators.note: involved in means caught up inside, so the fellow goes within the word for robbery

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: A man mixed up in a theft turns out to be a thrill-seeker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fellow' is a college don, a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone devoted to pursuing enjoyment is a sybarite.

clue.text: End of road more likely to produce skids — hence, more hazardous

indicators.note: End of picks out the final letter of the word road

parts.note: icier roads are more slippery, so more likely to cause skids

explanation.surface: Bad road conditions grow riskier as icy patches cause cars to skid.
explanation.definitionFit: Riskier, more uncertain, as a game of chance is.

clue.text: Spoil girl in Spanish resort

explanation.surface: A girl is ruined on holiday in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A Costa del Sol town is a popular Spanish holiday destination.

clue.text: Pharaoh twice expressed disapproval

indicators.note: twice means the pharaoh's name is written two times

parts.note: Tut, short for Tutankhamun, is the famous Egyptian pharaoh

explanation.surface: An Egyptian king said no and no again.
explanation.definitionFit: The doubled click of the tongue is an exclamation of mild reproach.

clue.text: A quiet dean, sadly not up to it

indicators.note: sadly means in a sorry state, so the letters are put in disorder

explanation.surface: A subdued college head is regrettably unequal to the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Insufficient for the task; not good enough.

clue.text: Queen going by railway in work by Hughes or work by Steinbeck

indicators.note: in means placed within, so the queen and railway go inside the poem's title

parts.note: Crow is a poetry collection by Ted Hughes

indicators.note: going by means travelling next to, so railway follows the queen

parts.note: Anne was a Queen of Great Britain

explanation.surface: A queen takes the train inside one literary work or another.
explanation.definitionFit: A 1945 novel by the American author is set among Monterey sardine canneries.

clue.text: "A powerful feller!" Bond observed

parts.note: a chain is a bond or fetter

explanation.surface: James Bond remarked on a strong man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feller' looks like a fellow; it means something that fells trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A motor-driven toothed cutting tool fells trees with great force.

clue.text: Cockney ballet, serene and graceful?

indicators.note: a Cockney (London East End) accent says the vowel of lake like the vowel of like

parts.note: Swan Lake is the ballet by Tchaikovsky

explanation.surface: A Londoner's ballet performance is calm and elegant.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the working-class accent of East London, where 'lake' sounds like 'like'.
explanation.definitionFit: A swan glides calmly and elegantly, so resembling one means poised.

clue.text: One day getting caught imbibing wine-that's typical of monks

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the wine goes inside the other pieces
getting means acquiring, so caught follows the day

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

explanation.surface: Someone is caught drinking wine one day, as monks typically do.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to life in a religious community of brothers, cloistered and disciplined.

clue.text: Expression when meeting an awkward situation

definitions.meaning: a formal greeting on being introduced

explanation.definitionFit: The formal greeting on introduction doubles as the phrase for a pretty kettle of fish, a predicament.

clue.text: Jolly part of Weimar in East Germany

indicators.note: part of signals that the letters lie within the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: A cheerful bit of Weimar in what was East Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' looks like an adjective; it is old naval slang for a Royal Marine. 'Germany' completes the surface picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Jolly is traditional Royal Navy slang for a sea soldier.

clue.text: A girl, meeting another, raised capital…

parts.note: Vi is a girl's name, short for Violet

indicators.note: raised means lifted up, so in a down clue the second name is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Two girls meet and bring up something important.
explanation.definitionFit: Austria's chief city is its seat of government.

clue.text: … capital provided articles on poles

parts.note: a and the are the indefinite and definite articles
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Wealth secured by putting items on sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek seat of government is that country's chief city.

clue.text: Holiday centre on island found by an ancient Greek

indicators.note: centre picks out the middle letter of the word Holiday

explanation.surface: A holiday resort on an island discovered by a classical Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a Hellenic people of antiquity, from the region of that name.

clue.text: Etching that shows tree top in a curious setting

indicators.note: in means placed within, so the tree's top letter goes inside

parts.note: quaint means curious or oddly old-fashioned

indicators.note: top picks out the first letter of the word tree

explanation.surface: A print shows a treetop within a strange background.
explanation.definitionFit: A method of intaglio printmaking giving tonal effects like watercolour is a form of etched print.

clue.text: Literary dean's birds

definitions.meaning: belonging to Jonathan Swift, Dean of St Patrick's in Dublin and author of Gulliver's Travels

explanation.definitionFit: The author-clergyman's surname with a possessive matches the plural of fast aerial birds.

clue.text: A nice pet playing a game

indicators.note: playing means frolicking about, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A sweet pet romps about.
explanation.definitionFit: A card game for one player, also called solitaire.
